body.target_estimand: At a fixed admissible query \(z_0\) and for \(\mathbb P_{z_0}\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}(z_0)\), the target is \(\tau(z_0)=\sum_{s=1}^{S}\pi_s\mathbb E_{\mathbb P_{z_0}}[B_{si}(1)-B_{si}(0)]\). For a joint panel law \(P\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}\), this conditional interpretation is asserted only for \(P\)-almost every query \(z_0\).
body.estimand_functional: At a fixed admissible query \(z_0\), consistency and event-date transport identify \(\tau(z_0)=\sum_s\pi_s\{\mathbb E_{\mathbb P_{z_0}}B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}-m_s(z_{0s})\}\) for every \(\mathbb P_{z_0}\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}(z_0)\). For \(0<\lambda\le1\), the deterministic fixed-design experiment supplies the conditional optimal-recovery bound, while random-design MSE and honest expected-length bounds and converses are uniform over this fixed-query class; the marginal squared-risk scale is \(R_\star=R_{\mathrm{or}}\vee N^{-\lambda}\), with the independent-calendar spacing replacement on \(\mathcal M^{\mathrm{iid}}_{N,T,\mathbf n}(z_0)\). The feasible interval uses whole-unit concentration and no calendar-score branch. For every joint panel law, its regular conditional kernel belongs to the fixed-query class for almost every query, and only there do the causal risk and coverage conclusions transfer. No supremum is taken over panel-specific values of a regular conditional law at a null query, no lower local modulus is assumed, and no headline result is claimed for \(\lambda>1\).

sampling_model.design: The pointwise statistical model is the kernel class \(\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}(z_0)\) at a fixed admissible query. For each cohort and date, the exact pre-event path has a density between \(c_X\) and \(C_X\) for Lebesgue-almost every design point, uniformly over these kernels, and each cohort's design sequence is geometrically beta mixing. The independent-calendar subclass imposes independence only on design dates under the fixed-query kernel. For a joint panel law, these conditions and all conclusions are asserted only at almost every query supplied by its regular conditional law.
sampling_model.units: Each cohort supplies \(n_s\) replicated untreated blocks per date and \(n_s\) treated event outcomes. Under a fixed-query kernel and conditional on the exact design, unit histories are independent across units and have the stated conditional means. Dependence across all training dates and the event outcome within one unit history remains unrestricted; inference treats that whole history as one bounded observation.
sampling_model.treatment: Consistency identifies observed event wealth with treated potential wealth. Event-date transport separately equates the unobserved untreated event mean with the historical regression at the realized path. Neither fixed-query design regularity nor design-conditional centering establishes this causal equality, and the panel-law interpretation is only query-almost-everywhere.
sampling_model.overlap: Every fixed query admitted to \(\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}(z_0)\) is at least \(\delta_0\) from the cube boundary. Exact fixed-design recovery can be easier than an anchor bandwidth suggests when a site equals the query. The regular donor-location converse requires \(\delta_0<1/2\), because otherwise the admissible displacement can collapse.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Only the event query is generated: deterministic donor folds produce projected means, and the full stacked covariance retains cross-coordinate, cross-horizon, and cross-cohort dependence. At a fixed query, donors are independent of the entire joint design-response-event panel, so further design conditioning preserves donor independence from unit histories. For \(0<\lambda\le1\), local-constant weights are nonnegative with unit absolute mass; whole-unit concentration is therefore sufficient and avoids deconvolution, calendar-score studentization, and response-mixing assumptions.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Gaussian convex-class theory links linear-functional minimax risk to a known-experiment modulus; it does not supply the bounded replicated-response and generated-query product experiment used here.
Its estimated-minimizer results use sample splitting and strong convexity, making location error second order rather than a rough-Holder external-query modulus.
Its generated-covariate expansion attaches an estimated coordinate to every training row, unlike the exact historical design and generated event query here.
Its replicated errors-in-variables experiment contaminates every latent training coordinate and requires deconvolution, which is absent under center-only generation.
The classical random-design Holder benchmark supplies ordinary smoothing context but not query-conditional spacing or a generated donor center.
Pointwise local-polynomial minimax theory motivates the anchor smoother but not the bounded product-experiment nearest-site frontier.
Optimal local-polynomial kernels concern ordinary pointwise asymptotic efficiency; the present result establishes only rate constants for a generated-query product experiment.
Random-design sup-norm sharp estimation addresses global loss and design adaptation, not conditional nearest-site recovery at an external generated query.
Classical nonparametric errors-in-variables contaminates all regression covariates, so its deconvolution rates do not govern the center-only design used here.
Generated-regressor asymptotic variance uses smooth semiparametric expansions; it does not cover the nonsmooth rough-Holder query modulus or its minimax converse.
Honest confidence-interval adaptation impossibility motivates fixing the Holder radius and smoothness rather than claiming adaptation across classes.
Ordered moduli characterize confidence intervals for linear functionals in known Gaussian experiments; the current interval must additionally cover generated-center error.
Bias-aware ordinary-regression intervals combine worst-case bias and stochastic calibration but contain no external full-covariance donor query.
Dependent-data resampling is not invoked: the repaired theorem uses whole-unit bounded-range concentration and design mixing only for anchor occupancy.
Many-control panel asymptotics motivate cross-unit replication but do not provide the generated-query optimal-recovery frontier.
Dependent synthetic-control prediction intervals address dependent innovations and estimated weights; the repaired interval instead uses unit-history concentration and no calendar-block calibration.
Conformal synthetic-control inference targets robust prediction coverage under a different exchangeability/time-series architecture, not full-covariance generated-query expected-length minimaxity.
The synthetic-control review motivates consistency and data-architecture transparency but does not validate the event-date counterfactual transport equality used for causal identification.
The longitudinal and panel causal-model survey locates the identifying assumptions; it does not derive the conditional generated-proxy minimax or honest-length frontier.

body.tldr: The paper delivers a fixed-query minimax and honest-length frontier for the rough Holder regime \(0<\lambda\le1\), where \(\kappa=\lambda\). At each admissible query \(z_0\), all uniform random-design statements are over the named conditional-kernel class \(\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}(z_0)\); a separate bridge transfers them to each causal panel law only for almost every realized query. Consistency and the explicitly untestable event-date transport equality identify the cohort-weighted buy-and-hold contrast. The nonredundant rate channels are treated replication, query-conditional calendar spacing, and full-covariance donor location. The feasible interval concentrates independent whole-unit histories and has no calendar-score branch. Conditional design independence removes the geometric-mixing logarithm. Higher-order signed-weight stability for \(\lambda>1\), uniform-in-query claims, and exact phase-intersection constants remain open.

project_justification.gap: Classical fixed-point regression does not combine replicated sites with an external full-covariance generated query, and a panel-law regular conditional distribution is not defined pointwise at query-null values. Existing ordinary-regression and synthetic-control intervals also do not justify globally design-selected calendar scores as independent blocks.
project_justification.niche: Historical paths can be recorded exactly while only the event-date counterfactual path is synthesized from donors. A named fixed-query kernel class makes the statistical frontier version invariant, while an almost-everywhere bridge keeps the causal panel interpretation honest. In the rough Holder regime this separates exact-design recovery, query-conditional spacing, donor-location uncertainty, and the untestable causal transport equality.
project_justification.fill: The note defines \(\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}(z_0)\) using pointwise conditional density, design-mixing, centering, donor-factorization, ellipticity, support, and causal restrictions at an admissible query. It proves conditional, marginal, and honest-length rate frontiers for \(0<\lambda\le1\) over that class and transfers them to every panel law for almost every query. A nearest-site rule and an anchor/extrapolation rule attain the risk rates. The honest interval uses whole-unit bounded-range concentration, generated-center bias calibration, and total fallbacks; matching lower bounds use explicit treated, spacing, and overlapping full-covariance donor pairs.

body.related_work: Donoho (1994) relates a linear-functional modulus to minimax recovery in a known Gaussian convex experiment; the conditional theorem instead constructs a bounded replicated-response product experiment with an external full-covariance query, nearest-site geometry, and a separate almost-everywhere causal bridge. Akhavan, Gogolashvili, and Tsybakov (2024) study independently estimated minimizers under strong convexity, making center error second order rather than a rough-Holder donor modulus. Stone (1982), Fan (1993), Fan et al. (1997), and Gaiffas (2007) provide ordinary Holder, pointwise local-polynomial, kernel-efficiency, and random-design sup-norm benchmarks; none supplies a fixed-query replicated-panel frontier with generated location. Mammen, Rothe, and Schienle (2012), Delaigle, Hall, and Meister (2008), and Fan and Truong (1993) perturb every training coordinate, unlike the exact historical design here; Hahn and Ridder (2013) gives smooth generated-regressor expansions rather than this nonsmooth modulus. Armstrong and Kolesar (2018, 2020) provide ordered-modulus and bias-aware ordinary-regression interval benchmarks, while Low (1997) motivates fixing the smoothness class rather than claiming adaptation. Cattaneo, Feng, and Titiunik (2021), Kunsch (1989), and Chernozhukov, Wuthrich, and Zhu (2021) concern dependent prediction, resampling, or conformal architectures; none is used for calendar calibration here, because the repaired interval concentrates independent whole-unit histories. Ferman (2021) motivates many-control replication. Abadie (2021) and Arkhangelsky and Imbens (2024) frame panel causal assumptions but neither validates event-date transport nor supplies the fixed-query statistical frontier.
body.interpretation: The fixed-query class separates exact-site geometry from uncertainty in a generated donor query without selecting arbitrary null versions of a panel regular conditional law. Query-conditional density and design mixing ensure that an admissible query cannot systematically select an unregulated design hole. Donor uncertainty dominates when \(N^{-\lambda}\) exceeds treated replication and spacing. For any causal panel law, this interpretation transfers only at almost every realized query. Inference needs no calendar response mixing: after fixing the admissible query, selected design, and donors, it concentrates across independent unit histories while allowing arbitrary temporal response dependence within a unit.
body.technical_internal_limitation: Every constructive headline is restricted to \(0<\lambda\le1\) and to fixed admissible queries in \(\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}(z_0)\); panel-law statements hold only almost everywhere in the query and are not uniform-in-query bands. For \(\lambda>1\), higher-order fixed-design recovery uses signed weights whose conditional stochastic norm is not controlled by the present assumptions. Geometric conditional design mixing retains the logarithmic spacing penalty; only conditional design independence yields the no-log term. The donor converse requires \(B^4>(Sd)^2\) and \(\delta_0<1/2\). The unit-history interval is rate-optimal but conservative, and exact phase-intersection constants remain open.
body.honest_scope: Event-date transport is an untestable causal restriction. Query-conditional density and design mixing are observed-law restrictions encoded pointwise in the fixed-query kernel class, while design-conditional centering is a separate response condition. Donor-panel separation factors donors from the complete joint panel and leaves dependence within each unit's training-event history unrestricted. Risk, coverage, and expected-length statements are uniform over \(\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}(z_0)\) at each admissible fixed query; for a joint panel law they transfer only for almost every query, with no claim at a null conditional version. The interval uses no calendar-score branch or estimated-variance division. Higher smoothness, growing dimension, adaptation, uniform-in-query bands, and exact constants are outside scope.
